explanation: I found no Mathlib declaration matching this result, and I did not run a search for one. I decided from the statement itself. The theorem is a custom real-variable inequality: an existential bound that holds uniformly in r, α, δ and H. Its left side is a specific product of terms built from (rα)⁻¹ and (rδ)⁻¹, and the hypotheses tie α, δ and H together. The bound was made for the Godement–Siegel estimate in this library, so it is not the kind of general statement Mathlib collects. The proof is a long hand-built chain of elementary inequalities (`Real.sqrt_le_sqrt`, `inv_anti₀`, `pow_le_pow_left₀`, `gcongr`, and a library lemma `sqrt_le_one_add`), with no single lemma doing the main work. Any proof from Mathlib would need many such steps, far more than the two lines allowed, so the result does not count as a duplicate or a special case.
